CNBC live updates via search summary (article 403) — Dow third straight loss Sep 24; 10Y 5.225% highest since 2007; stocks off lows on Reuters report of US-Iran phased Hormuz deal talks (Sep 24)

semis.why: SOXX +1.28% pre on AI-demand news (Meta Muse traction, Akamai-Anthropic $11.6bn), 17/18 green, Samsung +3.2%. Added beyond the gap: SOXX has closed above the 20:00 ref five straight sessions (09-18..09-24) through a 19-year-high 10Y, so the yield channel is not binding chips right now. Mild. Don't add: +9% 5d, +10.9% vs 50d median, Thu vol 0.65x, MU print 09-30

big_tech.why: QQQ +0.59% pre is mostly its chip weights; megacap cluster median only +0.25% (MSFT flat, META +0.1% at RSI 81). Mild, less than semis; most exposed if the 10Y re-breaks 5.22%

sg_banks.why: STI closed +0.51% at 5710.65, exactly on its 20d; Monday close after a weekend where the Iran-deal report can firm or die; no SG catalyst before MAS MPS by 10-14

market.why: SPY +0.34% pre, held between oil -2.2% (helps) and the 10Y at 5.16% (hurts); Dow on a fourth losing week; durable goods 20:30 SGT + Williams/Schmid/Hammack speaking

summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have; don't add chips or big tech after a 9% five-day run in chips and before Micron reports next Wednesday. I lean mildly up tonight, with low confidence.
summary.where_we_are: Friday 19:03 SGT / 07:03 ET. US pre-market; the open is at 21:30 SGT. Singapore is closed until Monday. August durable-goods orders come out at 20:30 SGT, and three Fed officials (Williams, Schmid, Hammack) speak during the session (Investing.com/Reuters, Sep 25).
summary.macro_attribution: Oil moved most overnight: US crude is down 2.2% to $93 (tape) after a report that US and Iranian negotiators are weighing a phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz (CNBC citing Reuters, Sep 24; seen only as a search summary, article not opened). The 10-year Treasury yield is flat at 5.16% (tape) after touching its highest level since 2007 on Thursday. The lean depends on that yield not breaking back above about 5.22%; cheaper oil helps but is not the bet.
what_happened: Chip stocks are up 1.3% before the open, with 17 of 18 names higher, led by Samsung (+3.2% in Seoul) and AXT, which makes compound-semiconductor wafers (+3.6%) (tape). Pre-market prices carry no volume, so this is thin until the open confirms it.
Chips have run 9% in five sessions and sit about 11% above their 50-day average (tape). Thursday's +2% close came on only 0.65x normal volume: a drift higher, not a stampede.
Futures are up on AI-demand news: traction for Meta's Muse app, and Akamai +21% on an $11.6bn cloud deal with Anthropic (Investing.com/Reuters, Sep 25 05:50 ET).
Big tech is barely moving: Microsoft flat, Meta +0.1% with its momentum gauge (RSI) at 81, which is stretched (tape). The Nasdaq-100's gain is mostly its chip weights.
Singapore banks closed up 0.8% (median) and the STI up 0.5% to 5,711, right on its 20-day average (tape). Their next close is Monday.

per_group.semis: Slightly up, mildly. The gap rides the same AI-demand news that has driven the whole run, and chips have closed above their 20:00 SGT price in each of the last five sessions even with 19-year-high yields. That streak, not the gap, is the bet; Friday profit-taking before Micron's report is the risk.
per_group.big_tech: Slightly up, less than chips. The index gain rides its chip weights; the megacaps themselves are flat and are the most exposed if the 10-year yield climbs.
per_group.sg_banks: Flat into Monday. The index sits right on its 20-day average, and weekend news on the Iran talks can cut either way.
per_group.market: Flat. The S&P 500 is caught between falling oil, which helps, and a 10-year yield above 5%, which hurts; the Dow is heading for a fourth losing week.

change_my_mind: The 10-year yield closes back above Thursday's 5.22% high: big tech and the whole market turn slightly down.
Chips give back the whole pre-market gain in the first hour on heavy volume: chips slightly down (profit-taking before Micron).
A hot durable-goods number at 20:30 SGT plus hawkish Fed speakers pushing yields up: the whole market slightly down.
The Iran deal is confirmed and crude drops below $90: the whole market slightly up.
summary.confidence: chips have moved about 2% a day in either direction this week, and the only thing I add beyond the gap is a five-session streak that can end any day.
summary.cant_know: Whether the Iran-deal report firms up or dies over the weekend, and what three Fed speakers say mid-session.
summary.the_call: Up, mildly. The S&P 500 ends roughly flat to a little higher. Chips lead again; Microsoft and Meta barely move. Singapore banks drift flat into Monday.
